sentence: Bacteria (i/bækˈtɪəriə/; singular: bacterium) constitute a large domain of prokaryotic microorganisms.
label: sentence

sentence: Typically a few micrometres in length, bacteria have a number of shapes, ranging from spheres to rods and spirals.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria were among the first life forms to appear on Earth, and are present in most of its habitats.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria inhabit soil, water, acidic hot springs, radioactive waste, and the deep portions of Earth's crust.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria also live in symbiotic and parasitic relationships with plants and animals.
label: sentence

sentence: They are also known to have flourished in manned spacecraft.
label: sentence

sentence: There are typically 40 million bacterial cells in a gram of soil and a million bacterial cells in a millilitre of fresh water.
label: sentence

sentence: There are approximately 5×1030 bacteria on Earth, forming a biomass which exceeds that of all plants and animals.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria are vital in recycling nutrients, with many of the stages in nutrient cycles dependent on these organisms, such as the fixation of nitrogen from the atmosphere and putrefaction.
label: sentence

sentence: In the biological communities surrounding hydrothermal vents and cold seeps, bacteria provide the nutrients needed to sustain life by converting dissolved compounds, such as hydrogen sulphide and methane, to energy.
label: sentence

sentence: On 17 March 2013, researchers reported data that suggested bacterial life forms thrive in the Mariana Trench, which with a depth of up to 11 kilometres is the deepest part of the Earth's oceans.
label: sentence

sentence: Other researchers reported related studies that microbes thrive inside rocks up to 580 metres below the sea floor under 2.6 kilometres of ocean off the coast of the northwestern United States.
label: sentence

sentence: According to one of the researchers, "You can find microbes everywhere — they're extremely adaptable to conditions, and survive wherever they are."
label: sentence

sentence: There are approximately ten times as many bacterial cells in the human flora as there are human cells in the body, with the largest number of the human flora being in the gut flora, and a large number on the skin.
label: sentence

sentence: The vast majority of the bacteria in the body are rendered harmless by the protective effects of the immune system, and some are beneficial.
label: sentence

sentence: However, several species of bacteria are pathogenic and cause infectious diseases, including cholera, syphilis, anthrax, leprosy, and bubonic plague.
label: sentence

sentence: The most common fatal bacterial diseases are respiratory infections, with tuberculosis alone killing about 2 million people per year, mostly in sub-Saharan Africa.
label: sentence

sentence: In developed countries, antibiotics are used to treat bacterial infections and are also used in farming, making antibiotic resistance a growing problem.
label: sentence

sentence: In industry, bacteria are important in sewage treatment and the breakdown of oil spills, the production of cheese and yogurt through fermentation, and the recovery of gold, palladium, copper and other metals in the mining sector, as well as in biotechnology, and the manufacture of antibiotics and other chemicals.
label: sentence

sentence: Once regarded as plants constituting the class Schizomycetes, bacteria are now classified as prokaryotes.
label: sentence

sentence: Unlike cells of animals and other eukaryotes, bacterial cells do not contain a nucleus and rarely harbour membrane-bound organelles.
label: sentence

sentence: Although the term bacteria traditionally included all prokaryotes, the scientific classification changed after the discovery in the 1990s that prokaryotes consist of two very different groups of organisms that evolved from an ancient common ancestor.
label: sentence

sentence: These evolutionary domains are called Bacteria and Archaea.
label: sentence

sentence: The ancestors of modern bacteria were unicellular microorganisms that were the first forms of life to appear on Earth, about 4 billion years ago.
label: sentence

sentence: For about 3 billion years, most organisms were microscopic, and bacteria and archaea were the dominant forms of life.
label: sentence

sentence: In 2008, fossils of macroorganisms were discovered and named as the Francevillian biota.
label: sentence

sentence: Although bacterial fossils exist, such as stromatolites, their lack of distinctive morphology prevents them from being used to examine the history of bacterial evolution, or to date the time of origin of a particular bacterial species.
label: sentence

sentence: However, gene sequences can be used to reconstruct the bacterial phylogeny, and these studies indicate that bacteria diverged first from the archaeal/eukaryotic lineage.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria were also involved in the second great evolutionary divergence, that of the archaea and eukaryotes.
label: sentence

sentence: Here, eukaryotes resulted from the entering of ancient bacteria into endosymbiotic associations with the ancestors of eukaryotic cells, which were themselves possibly related to the Archaea.
label: sentence

sentence: This involved the engulfment by proto-eukaryotic cells of alphaproteobacterial symbionts to form either mitochondria or hydrogenosomes, which are still found in all known Eukarya (sometimes in highly reduced form, e.g.
label: sentence

sentence: in ancient "amitochondrial" protozoa).
label: sentence

sentence: Later on, some eukaryotes that already contained mitochondria also engulfed cyanobacterial-like organisms.
label: sentence

sentence: This led to the formation of chloroplasts in algae and plants.
label: sentence

sentence: There are also some algae that originated from even later endosymbiotic events.
label: sentence

sentence: Here, eukaryotes engulfed a eukaryotic algae that developed into a "second-generation" plastid.
label: sentence

sentence: This is known as secondary endosymbiosis.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria display a wide diversity of shapes and sizes, called morphologies.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacterial cells are about one-tenth the size of eukaryotic cells and are typically 0.5–5.0 micrometres in length.
label: sentence

sentence: However, a few species are visible to the unaided eye — for example, Thiomargarita namibiensis is up to half a millimetre long and Epulopiscium fishelsoni reaches 0.7 mm.
label: sentence

sentence: Among the smallest bacteria are members of the genus Mycoplasma, which measure only 0.3 micrometres, as small as the largest viruses.
label: sentence

sentence: Some bacteria may be even smaller, but these ultramicrobacteria are not well-studied.
label: sentence

sentence: Most bacterial species are either spherical, called cocci (sing.
label: sentence

sentence: coccus, from Greek kókkos, grain, seed), or rod-shaped, called bacilli (sing.
label: sentence

sentence: bacillus, from Latin baculus, stick).
label: sentence

sentence: Elongation is associated with swimming.
label: sentence

sentence: Some bacteria, called vibrio, are shaped like slightly curved rods or comma-shaped; others can be spiral-shaped, called spirilla, or tightly coiled, called spirochaetes.
label: sentence

sentence: A small number of species even have tetrahedral or cuboidal shapes.
label: sentence

sentence: More recently, some bacteria were discovered deep under Earth's crust that grow as branching filamentous types with a star-shaped cross-section.
label: sentence

sentence: The large surface area to volume ratio of this morphology may give these bacteria an advantage in nutrient-poor environments.
label: sentence

sentence: This wide variety of shapes is determined by the bacterial cell wall and cytoskeleton, and is important because it can influence the ability of bacteria to acquire nutrients, attach to surfaces, swim through liquids and escape predators.
label: sentence

sentence: Many bacterial species exist simply as single cells, others associate in characteristic patterns: Neisseria form diploids (pairs), Streptococcus form chains, and Staphylococcus group together in "bunch of grapes" clusters.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria can also be elongated to form filaments, for example the Actinobacteria.
label: sentence

sentence: Filamentous bacteria are often surrounded by a sheath that contains many individual cells.
label: sentence

sentence: Certain types, such as species of the genus Nocardia, even form complex, branched filaments, similar in appearance to fungal mycelia.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria often attach to surfaces and form dense aggregations called biofilms or bacterial mats.
label: sentence

sentence: These films can range from a few micrometers in thickness to up to half a meter in depth, and may contain multiple species of bacteria, protists and archaea.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria living in biofilms display a complex arrangement of cells and extracellular components, forming secondary structures, such as microcolonies, through which there are networks of channels to enable better diffusion of nutrients.
label: sentence

sentence: In natural environments, such as soil or the surfaces of plants, the majority of bacteria are bound to surfaces in biofilms.
label: sentence

sentence: Biofilms are also important in medicine, as these structures are often present during chronic bacterial infections or in infections of implanted medical devices, and bacteria protected within biofilms are much harder to kill than individual isolated bacteria.
label: sentence

sentence: Even more complex morphological changes are sometimes possible.
label: sentence

sentence: For example, when starved of amino acids, Myxobacteria detect surrounding cells in a process known as quorum sensing, migrate toward each other, and aggregate to form fruiting bodies up to 500 micrometres long and containing approximately 100,000 bacterial cells.
label: sentence

sentence: In these fruiting bodies, the bacteria perform separate tasks; this type of cooperation is a simple type of multicellular organisation.
label: sentence

sentence: For example, about one in 10 cells migrate to the top of these fruiting bodies and differentiate into a specialised dormant state called myxospores, which are more resistant to drying and other adverse environmental conditions than are ordinary cells.
label: sentence

sentence: The bacterial cell is surrounded by a cell membrane (also known as a lipid, cytoplasmic or plasma membrane).
label: sentence

sentence: This membrane encloses the contents of the cell and acts as a barrier to hold nutrients, proteins and other essential components of the cytoplasm within the cell.
label: sentence

sentence: As they are prokaryotes, bacteria do not usually have membrane-bound organelles in their cytoplasm, and thus contain few large intracellular structures.
label: sentence

sentence: They lack a true nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplasts and the other organelles present in eukaryotic cells.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria were once seen as simple bags of cytoplasm, but structures such as the prokaryotic cytoskeleton and the localization of proteins to specific locations within the cytoplasm that give bacteria some complexity have been discovered.
label: sentence

sentence: These subcellular levels of organization have been called "bacterial hyperstructures".
label: sentence

sentence: Many important biochemical reactions, such as energy generation, use concentration gradients across membranes.
label: sentence

sentence: The general lack of internal membranes in bacteria means reactions such as electron transport occur across the cell membrane between the cytoplasm and the periplasmic space.
label: sentence

sentence: However, in many photosynthetic bacteria the plasma membrane is highly folded and fills most of the cell with layers of light-gathering membrane.
label: sentence

sentence: These light-gathering complexes may even form lipid-enclosed structures called chlorosomes in green sulfur bacteria.
label: sentence

sentence: Other proteins import nutrients across the cell membrane, or expel undesired molecules from the cytoplasm.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria do not have a membrane-bound nucleus, and their genetic material is typically a single circular DNA chromosome located in the cytoplasm in an irregularly shaped body called the nucleoid.
label: sentence

sentence: The nucleoid contains the chromosome with its associated proteins and RNA.
label: sentence

sentence: The phylum Planctomycetes and candidate phylum Poribacteria may be exceptions to the general absence of internal membranes in bacteria, because they appear to have a double membrane around their nucleoids and contain other membrane-bound cellular structures.
label: sentence

sentence: Like all living organisms, bacteria contain ribosomes, often grouped in chains called polyribosomes, for the production of proteins, but the structure of the bacterial ribosome is different from that of eukaryotes and Archaea.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacterial ribosomes have a sedimentation rate of 70S (measured in Svedberg units): their subunits have rates of 30S and 50S.
label: sentence

sentence: Some antibiotics bind specifically to 70S ribosomes and inhibit bacterial protein synthesis.
label: sentence

sentence: Those antibiotics kill bacteria without affecting the larger 80S ribosomes of eukaryotic cells and without harming the host.
label: sentence

sentence: Some bacteria produce intracellular nutrient storage granules for later use, such as glycogen, polyphosphate, sulfur or polyhydroxyalkanoates.
label: sentence

sentence: Certain bacterial species, such as the photosynthetic Cyanobacteria, produce internal gas vesicles, which they use to regulate their buoyancy – allowing them to move up or down into water layers with different light intensities and nutrient levels.
label: sentence

sentence: Intracellular membranes called chromatophores are also found in membranes of phototrophic bacteria.
label: sentence

sentence: Used primarily for photosynthesis, they contain bacteriochlorophyll pigments and carotenoids.
label: sentence

sentence: An early idea was that bacteria might contain membrane folds termed mesosomes, but these were later shown to be artifacts produced by the chemicals used to prepare the cells for electron microscopy.
label: sentence

sentence: Inclusions are considered to be nonliving components of the cell that do not possess metabolic activity and are not bounded by membranes.
label: sentence

sentence: The most common inclusions are glycogen, lipid droplets, crystals, and pigments.
label: sentence

sentence: Volutin granules are cytoplasmic inclusions of complexed inorganic polyphosphate.
label: sentence

sentence: These granules are called metachromatic granules due to their displaying the metachromatic effect; they appear red or blue when stained with the blue dyes methylene blue or toluidine blue.
label: sentence

sentence: Gas vacuoles, which are freely permeable to gas, are membrane-bound vesicles present in some species of Cyanobacteria.
label: sentence

sentence: They allow the bacteria to control their buoyancy.
label: sentence

sentence: Microcompartments are widespread, membrane-bound organelles that are made of a protein shell that surrounds and encloses various enzymes.
label: sentence

sentence: Carboxysomes are bacterial microcompartments that contain enzymes involved in carbon fixation.
label: sentence

sentence: Magnetosomes are bacterial microcompartments, present in magnetotactic bacteria, that contain magnetic crystals.
label: sentence

sentence: In most bacteria, a cell wall is present on the outside of the cell membrane.
label: sentence

sentence: The cell membrane and cell wall comprise the cell envelope.
label: sentence

sentence: A common bacterial cell wall material is peptidoglycan (called "murein" in older sources), which is made from polysaccharide chains cross-linked by peptides containing D-amino acids.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacterial cell walls are different from the cell walls of plants and fungi, which are made of cellulose and chitin, respectively.
label: sentence

sentence: The cell wall of bacteria is also distinct from that of Archaea, which do not contain peptidoglycan.
label: sentence

sentence: The cell wall is essential to the survival of many bacteria, and the antibiotic penicillin is able to kill bacteria by inhibiting a step in the synthesis of peptidoglycan.
label: sentence

sentence: Gram-positive bacteria possess a thick cell wall containing many layers of peptidoglycan and teichoic acids.
label: sentence

sentence: In contrast, gram-negative bacteria have a relatively thin cell wall consisting of a few layers of peptidoglycan surrounded by a second lipid membrane containing lipopolysaccharides and lipoproteins.
label: sentence

sentence: Lipopolysaccharides, also called endotoxins, are composed of polysaccharides and lipid A that is responsible for much of the toxicity of gram-negative bacteria.
label: sentence

sentence: Most bacteria have the gram-negative cell wall, and only the Firmicutes and Actinobacteria have the alternative gram-positive arrangement.
label: sentence

sentence: These two groups were previously known as the low G+C and high G+C Gram-positive bacteria, respectively.
label: sentence

sentence: These differences in structure can produce differences in antibiotic susceptibility; for instance, vancomycin can kill only gram-positive bacteria and is ineffective against gram-negative pathogens, such as Haemophilus influenzae or Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
label: sentence

sentence: If the bacterial cell wall is entirely removed, it is called a protoplast, whereas if it is partially removed, it is called a spheroplast.
label: sentence

sentence: β-Lactam antibiotics, such as penicillin, inhibit the formation of peptidoglycan cross-links in the bacterial cell wall.
label: sentence

sentence: The enzyme lysozyme, found in human tears, also digests the cell wall of bacteria and is the body's main defense against eye infections.
label: sentence

sentence: Acid-fast bacteria, such as Mycobacteria, are resistant to decolorization by acids during staining procedures.
label: sentence

sentence: The high mycolic acid content of Mycobacteria, is responsible for the staining pattern of poor absorption followed by high retention.
label: sentence

sentence: The most common staining technique used to identify acid-fast bacteria is the Ziehl-Neelsen stain or acid-fast stain, in which the acid-fast bacilli are stained bright-red and stand out clearly against a blue background.
label: sentence

sentence: L-form bacteria are strains of bacteria that lack cell walls.
label: sentence

sentence: The main pathogenic bacteria in this class is Mycoplasma (not to be confused with Mycobacteria).
label: sentence

sentence: Fimbriae (sometimes called "attachment pili") are fine filaments of protein, usually 2–10 nanometres in diameter and up to several micrometers in length.
label: sentence

sentence: They are distributed over the surface of the cell, and resemble fine hairs when seen under the electron microscope.
label: sentence

sentence: Fimbriae are believed to be involved in attachment to solid surfaces or to other cells, and are essential for the virulence of some bacterial pathogens.
label: sentence

sentence: Pili (sing.
label: sentence

sentence: pilus) are cellular appendages, slightly larger than fimbriae, that can transfer genetic material between bacterial cells in a process called conjugation where they are called conjugation pili or "sex pili" (see bacterial genetics, below).
label: sentence

sentence: They can also generate movement where they are called type IV pili (see movement, below).
label: sentence

sentence: Certain genera of Gram-positive bacteria, such as Bacillus, Clostridium, Sporohalobacter, Anaerobacter, and Heliobacterium, can form highly resistant, dormant structures called endospores.
label: sentence

sentence: In almost all cases, one endospore is formed and this is not a reproductive process, although Anaerobacter can make up to seven endospores in a single cell.
label: sentence

sentence: Endospores have a central core of cytoplasm containing DNA and ribosomes surrounded by a cortex layer and protected by an impermeable and rigid coat.
label: sentence

sentence: Dipicolinic acid is a chemical compound that composes 5% to 15% of the dry weight of bacterial spores.
label: sentence

sentence: It is implicated as responsible for the heat resistance of the endospore.
label: sentence

sentence: Endospores show no detectable metabolism and can survive extreme physical and chemical stresses, such as high levels of UV light, gamma radiation, detergents, disinfectants, heat, freezing, pressure, and desiccation.
label: sentence

sentence: In this dormant state, these organisms may remain viable for millions of years, and endospores even allow bacteria to survive exposure to the vacuum and radiation in space.
label: sentence

sentence: According to scientist Dr. Steinn Sigurdsson, "There are viable bacterial spores that have been found that are 40 million years old on Earth — and we know they're very hardened to radiation."
label: sentence

sentence: Endospore-forming bacteria can also cause disease: for example, anthrax can be contracted by the inhalation of Bacillus anthracis endospores, and contamination of deep puncture wounds with Clostridium tetani endospores causes tetanus.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria exhibit an extremely wide variety of metabolic types.
label: sentence

sentence: The distribution of metabolic traits within a group of bacteria has traditionally been used to define their taxonomy, but these traits often do not correspond with modern genetic classifications.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacterial metabolism is classified into nutritional groups on the basis of three major criteria: the kind of energy used for growth, the source of carbon, and the electron donors used for growth.
label: sentence

sentence: An additional criterion of respiratory microorganisms are the electron acceptors used for aerobic or anaerobic respiration.
label: sentence

sentence: Carbon metabolism in bacteria is either heterotrophic, where organic carbon compounds are used as carbon sources, or autotrophic, meaning that cellular carbon is obtained by fixing carbon dioxide.
label: sentence

sentence: Heterotrophic bacteria include parasitic types.
label: sentence

sentence: Typical autotrophic bacteria are phototrophic cyanobacteria, green sulfur-bacteria and some purple bacteria, but also many chemolithotrophic species, such as nitrifying or sulfur-oxidising bacteria.
label: sentence

sentence: Energy metabolism of bacteria is either based on phototrophy, the use of light through photosynthesis, or based on chemotrophy, the use of chemical substances for energy, which are mostly oxidised at the expense of oxygen or alternative electron acceptors (aerobic/anaerobic respiration).
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria are further divided into lithotrophs that use inorganic electron donors and organotrophs that use organic compounds as electron donors.
label: sentence

sentence: Chemotrophic organisms use the respective electron donors for energy conservation (by aerobic/anaerobic respiration or fermentation) and biosynthetic reactions (e.g., carbon dioxide fixation), whereas phototrophic organisms use them only for biosynthetic purposes.
label: sentence

sentence: Respiratory organisms use chemical compounds as a source of energy by taking electrons from the reduced substrate and transferring them to a terminal electron acceptor in a redox reaction.
label: sentence

sentence: This reaction releases energy that can be used to synthesise ATP and drive metabolism.
label: sentence

sentence: In aerobic organisms, oxygen is used as the electron acceptor.
label: sentence

sentence: In anaerobic organisms other inorganic compounds, such as nitrate, sulfate or carbon dioxide are used as electron acceptors.
label: sentence

sentence: This leads to the ecologically important processes of denitrification, sulfate reduction, and acetogenesis, respectively.
label: sentence

sentence: These processes are also important in biological responses to pollution; for example, sulfate-reducing bacteria are largely responsible for the production of the highly toxic forms of mercury (methyl- and dimethylmercury) in the environment.
label: sentence

sentence: Non-respiratory anaerobes use fermentation to generate energy and reducing power, secreting metabolic by-products (such as ethanol in brewing) as waste.
label: sentence

sentence: Facultative anaerobes can switch between fermentation and different terminal electron acceptors depending on the environmental conditions in which they find themselves.
label: sentence

sentence: Lithotrophic bacteria can use inorganic compounds as a source of energy.
label: sentence

sentence: Common inorganic electron donors are hydrogen, carbon monoxide, ammonia (leading to nitrification), ferrous iron and other reduced metal ions, and several reduced sulfur compounds.
label: sentence

sentence: In unusual circumstances, the gas methane can be used by methanotrophic bacteria as both a source of electrons and a substrate for carbon anabolism.
label: sentence

sentence: In both aerobic phototrophy and chemolithotrophy, oxygen is used as a terminal electron acceptor, whereas under anaerobic conditions inorganic compounds are used instead.
label: sentence

sentence: Most lithotrophic organisms are autotrophic, whereas organotrophic organisms are heterotrophic.
label: sentence

sentence: Regardless of the type of metabolic process they employ, the majority of bacteria are able to take in raw materials only in the form of relatively small molecules, which enter the cell by diffusion or through molecular channels in cell membranes.
label: sentence

sentence: The Planctomycetes are the exception (as they are in possessing membranes around their nuclear material).
label: sentence

sentence: It has recently been shown that Gemmata obscuriglobus is able to take in large molecules via a process that in some ways resembles endocytosis, the process used by eukaryotic cells to engulf external items.
label: sentence

sentence: Unlike in multicellular organisms, increases in cell size (cell growth) and reproduction by cell division are tightly linked in unicellular organisms.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria grow to a fixed size and then reproduce through binary fission, a form of asexual reproduction.
label: sentence

sentence: Under optimal conditions, bacteria can grow and divide extremely rapidly, and bacterial populations can double as quickly as every 9.8 minutes.
label: sentence

sentence: In cell division, two identical clone daughter cells are produced.
label: sentence

sentence: Some bacteria, while still reproducing asexually, form more complex reproductive structures that help disperse the newly formed daughter cells.
label: sentence

sentence: Examples include fruiting body formation by Myxobacteria and aerial hyphae formation by Streptomyces, or budding.
label: sentence

sentence: Budding involves a cell forming a protrusion that breaks away and produces a daughter cell.
label: sentence

sentence: In the laboratory, bacteria are usually grown using solid or liquid media.
label: sentence

sentence: Solid growth media, such as agar plates, are used to isolate pure cultures of a bacterial strain.
label: sentence

sentence: However, liquid growth media are used when measurement of growth or large volumes of cells are required.
label: sentence

sentence: Growth in stirred liquid media occurs as an even cell suspension, making the cultures easy to divide and transfer, although isolating single bacteria from liquid media is difficult.
label: sentence

sentence: The use of selective media (media with specific nutrients added or deficient, or with antibiotics added) can help identify specific organisms.
label: sentence

sentence: Most laboratory techniques for growing bacteria use high levels of nutrients to produce large amounts of cells cheaply and quickly.
label: sentence

sentence: However, in natural environments, nutrients are limited, meaning that bacteria cannot continue to reproduce indefinitely.
label: sentence

sentence: This nutrient limitation has led the evolution of different growth strategies (see r/K selection theory).
label: sentence

sentence: Some organisms can grow extremely rapidly when nutrients become available, such as the formation of algal (and cyanobacterial) blooms that often occur in lakes during the summer.
label: sentence

sentence: Other organisms have adaptations to harsh environments, such as the production of multiple antibiotics by Streptomyces that inhibit the growth of competing microorganisms.
label: sentence

sentence: In nature, many organisms live in communities (e.g., biofilms) that may allow for increased supply of nutrients and protection from environmental stresses.
label: sentence

sentence: These relationships can be essential for growth of a particular organism or group of organisms (syntrophy).
label: sentence

sentence: Bacterial growth follows four phases.
label: sentence

sentence: When a population of bacteria first enter a high-nutrient environment that allows growth, the cells need to adapt to their new environment.
label: sentence

sentence: The first phase of growth is the lag phase, a period of slow growth when the cells are adapting to the high-nutrient environment and preparing for fast growth.
label: sentence

sentence: The lag phase has high biosynthesis rates, as proteins necessary for rapid growth are produced.
label: sentence

sentence: The second phase of growth is the log phase, also known as the logarithmic or exponential phase.
label: sentence

sentence: The log phase is marked by rapid exponential growth.
label: sentence

sentence: The rate at which cells grow during this phase is known as the growth rate (k), and the time it takes the cells to double is known as the generation time (g).
label: sentence

sentence: During log phase, nutrients are metabolised at maximum speed until one of the nutrients is depleted and starts limiting growth.
label: sentence

sentence: The third phase of growth is the stationary phase and is caused by depleted nutrients.
label: sentence

sentence: The cells reduce their metabolic activity and consume non-essential cellular proteins.
label: sentence

sentence: The stationary phase is a transition from rapid growth to a stress response state and there is increased expression of genes involved in DNA repair, antioxidant metabolism and nutrient transport.
label: sentence

sentence: The final phase is the death phase where the bacteria run out of nutrients and die.
label: sentence

sentence: Most bacteria have a single circular chromosome that can range in size from only 160,000 base pairs in the endosymbiotic bacteria Candidatus Carsonella ruddii, to 12,200,000 base pairs in the soil-dwelling bacteria Sorangium cellulosum.
label: sentence

sentence: Spirochaetes of the genus Borrelia are a notable exception to this arrangement, with bacteria such as Borrelia burgdorferi, the cause of Lyme disease, containing a single linear chromosome.
label: sentence

sentence: The genes in bacterial genomes are usually a single continuous stretch of DNA and although several different types of introns do exist in bacteria, these are much rarer than in eukaryotes.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria, as asexual organisms, inherit identical copies of their parent's genes (i.e., they are clonal).
label: sentence

sentence: However, all bacteria can evolve by selection on changes to their genetic material DNA caused by genetic recombination or mutations.
label: sentence

sentence: Mutations come from errors made during the replication of DNA or from exposure to mutagens.
label: sentence

sentence: Mutation rates vary widely among different species of bacteria and even among different clones of a single species of bacteria.
label: sentence

sentence: Genetic changes in bacterial genomes come from either random mutation during replication or "stress-directed mutation", where genes involved in a particular growth-limiting process have an increased mutation rate.
label: sentence

sentence: Transduction of bacterial genes by bacteriophage appears to be a consequence of infrequent errors during intracellular assembly of virus particles, rather than a bacterial adaptation.
label: sentence

sentence: Conjugation, in the much-studied E. coli system is determined by plasmid genes, and is an adaptation for transferring copies of the plasmid from one bacterial host to another.
label: sentence

sentence: It is seldom that a conjugative plasmid integrates into the host bacterial chromosome, and subsequently transfers part of the host bacterial DNA to another bacterium.
label: sentence

sentence: Plasmid-mediated transfer of host bacterial DNA also appears to be an accidental process rather than a bacterial adaptation.
label: sentence

sentence: Transformation, unlike transduction or conjugation, depends on numerous bacterial gene products that specifically interact to perform this complex process, and thus transformation is clearly a bacterial adaptation for DNA transfer.
label: sentence

sentence: In order for a bacterium to bind, take up and recombine donor DNA into its own chromosome, it must first enter a special physiological state termed competence (see Natural competence).
label: sentence

sentence: In Bacillus subtilis, about 40 genes are required for the development of competence.
label: sentence

sentence: The length of DNA transferred during B. subtilis transformation can be between a third of a chromosome up to the whole chromosome.
label: sentence

sentence: Transformation appears to be common among bacterial species, and thus far at least 60 species are known to have the natural ability to become competent for transformation.
label: sentence

sentence: The development of competence in nature is usually associated with stressful environmental conditions, and seems to be an adaptation for facilitating repair of DNA damage in recipient cells.
label: sentence

sentence: In ordinary circumstances, transduction, conjugation, and transformation involve transfer of DNA between individual bacteria of the same species, but occasionally transfer may occur between individuals of different bacterial species and this may have significant consequences, such as the transfer of antibiotic resistance.
label: sentence

sentence: In such cases, gene acquisition from other bacteria or the environment is called horizontal gene transfer and may be common under natural conditions.
label: sentence

sentence: Gene transfer is particularly important in antibiotic resistance as it allows the rapid transfer of resistance genes between different pathogens.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteriophages are viruses that infect bacteria.
label: sentence

sentence: Many types of bacteriophage exist, some simply infect and lyse their host bacteria, while others insert into the bacterial chromosome.
label: sentence

sentence: A bacteriophage can contain genes that contribute to its host's phenotype: for example, in the evolution of Escherichia coli O157:H7 and Clostridium botulinum, the toxin genes in an integrated phage converted a harmless ancestral bacterium into a lethal pathogen.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria resist phage infection through restriction modification systems that degrade foreign DNA, and a system that uses CRISPR sequences to retain fragments of the genomes of phage that the bacteria have come into contact with in the past, which allows them to block virus replication through a form of RNA interference.
label: sentence

sentence: This CRISPR system provides bacteria with acquired immunity to infection.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacterial species differ in the number and arrangement of flagella on their surface; some have a single flagellum (monotrichous), a flagellum at each end (amphitrichous), clusters of flagella at the poles of the cell (lophotrichous), while others have flagella distributed over the entire surface of the cell (peritrichous).
label: sentence

sentence: The bacterial flagella is the best-understood motility structure in any organism and is made of about 20 proteins, with approximately another 30 proteins required for its regulation and assembly.
label: sentence

sentence: The flagellum is a rotating structure driven by a reversible motor at the base that uses the electrochemical gradient across the membrane for power.
label: sentence

sentence: This motor drives the motion of the filament, which acts as a propeller.
label: sentence

sentence: Classification seeks to describe the diversity of bacterial species by naming and grouping organisms based on similarities.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria can be classified on the basis of cell structure, cellular metabolism or on differences in cell components, such as DNA, fatty acids, pigments, antigens and quinones.
label: sentence

sentence: While these schemes allowed the identification and classification of bacterial strains, it was unclear whether these differences represented variation between distinct species or between strains of the same species.
label: sentence

sentence: This uncertainty was due to the lack of distinctive structures in most bacteria, as well as lateral gene transfer between unrelated species.
label: sentence

sentence: Due to lateral gene transfer, some closely related bacteria can have very different morphologies and metabolisms.
label: sentence

sentence: To overcome this uncertainty, modern bacterial classification emphasizes molecular systematics, using genetic techniques such as guanine cytosine ratio determination, genome-genome hybridization, as well as sequencing genes that have not undergone extensive lateral gene transfer, such as the rRNA gene.
label: sentence

sentence: Classification of bacteria is determined by publication in the International Journal of Systematic Bacteriology, and Bergey's Manual of Systematic Bacteriology.
label: sentence

sentence: The International Committee on Systematic Bacteriology (ICSB) maintains international rules for the naming of bacteria and taxonomic categories and for the ranking of them in the International Code of Nomenclature of Bacteria.
label: sentence

sentence: The term "bacteria" was traditionally applied to all microscopic, single-cell prokaryotes.
label: sentence

sentence: However, molecular systematics showed prokaryotic life to consist of two separate domains, originally called Eubacteria and Archaebacteria, but now called Bacteria and Archaea that evolved independently from an ancient common ancestor.
label: sentence

sentence: The archaea and eukaryotes are more closely related to each other than either is to the bacteria.
label: sentence

sentence: These two domains, along with Eukarya, are the basis of the three-domain system, which is currently the most widely used classification system in microbiolology.
label: sentence

sentence: However, due to the relatively recent introduction of molecular systematics and a rapid increase in the number of genome sequences that are available, bacterial classification remains a changing and expanding field.
label: sentence

sentence: For example, a few biologists argue that the Archaea and Eukaryotes evolved from Gram-positive bacteria.
label: sentence

sentence: The Gram stain, developed in 1884 by Hans Christian Gram, characterises bacteria based on the structural characteristics of their cell walls.
label: sentence

sentence: The thick layers of peptidoglycan in the "Gram-positive" cell wall stain purple, while the thin "Gram-negative" cell wall appears pink.
label: sentence

sentence: By combining morphology and Gram-staining, most bacteria can be classified as belonging to one of four groups (Gram-positive cocci, Gram-positive bacilli, Gram-negative cocci and Gram-negative bacilli).
label: sentence

sentence: Some organisms are best identified by stains other than the Gram stain, particularly mycobacteria or Nocardia, which show acid-fastness on Ziehl–Neelsen or similar stains.
label: sentence

sentence: Other organisms may need to be identified by their growth in special media, or by other techniques, such as serology.
label: sentence

sentence: As with bacterial classification, identification of bacteria is increasingly using molecular methods.
label: sentence

sentence: Diagnostics using DNA-based tools, such as polymerase chain reaction, are increasingly popular due to their specificity and speed, compared to culture-based methods.
label: sentence

sentence: These methods also allow the detection and identification of "viable but nonculturable" cells that are metabolically active but non-dividing.
label: sentence

sentence: However, even using these improved methods, the total number of bacterial species is not known and cannot even be estimated with any certainty.
label: sentence

sentence: Following present classification, there are a little less than 9,300 known species of prokaryotes, which includes bacteria and archaea; but attempts to estimate the true number of bacterial diversity have ranged from 107 to 109 total species – and even these diverse estimates may be off by many orders of magnitude.
label: sentence

sentence: Some species of bacteria kill and then consume other microorganisms, these species are called predatory bacteria.
label: sentence

sentence: These include organisms such as Myxococcus xanthus, which forms swarms of cells that kill and digest any bacteria they encounter.
label: sentence

sentence: Other bacterial predators either attach to their prey in order to digest them and absorb nutrients, such as Vampirovibrio chlorellavorus, or invade another cell and multiply inside the cytosol, such as Daptobacter.
label: sentence

sentence: These predatory bacteria are thought to have evolved from saprophages that consumed dead microorganisms, through adaptations that allowed them to entrap and kill other organisms.
label: sentence

sentence: Certain bacteria form close spatial associations that are essential for their survival.
label: sentence

sentence: One such mutualistic association, called interspecies hydrogen transfer, occurs between clusters of anaerobic bacteria that consume organic acids, such as butyric acid or propionic acid, and produce hydrogen, and methanogenic Archaea that consume hydrogen.
label: sentence

sentence: The bacteria in this association are unable to consume the organic acids as this reaction produces hydrogen that accumulates in their surroundings.
label: sentence

sentence: Only the intimate association with the hydrogen-consuming Archaea keeps the hydrogen concentration low enough to allow the bacteria to grow.
label: sentence

sentence: In soil, microorganisms that reside in the rhizosphere (a zone that includes the root surface and the soil that adheres to the root after gentle shaking) carry out nitrogen fixation, converting nitrogen gas to nitrogenous compounds.
label: sentence

sentence: This serves to provide an easily absorbable form of nitrogen for many plants, which cannot fix nitrogen themselves.
label: sentence

sentence: Many other bacteria are found as symbionts in humans and other organisms.
label: sentence

sentence: For example, the presence of over 1,000 bacterial species in the normal human gut flora of the intestines can contribute to gut immunity, synthesise vitamins, such as folic acid, vitamin K and biotin, convert sugars to lactic acid (see Lactobacillus), as well as fermenting complex undigestible carbohydrates.
label: sentence

sentence: The presence of this gut flora also inhibits the growth of potentially pathogenic bacteria (usually through competitive exclusion) and these beneficial bacteria are consequently sold as probiotic dietary supplements.
label: sentence

sentence: If bacteria form a parasitic association with other organisms, they are classed as pathogens.
label: sentence

sentence: Pathogenic bacteria are a major cause of human death and disease and cause infections such as tetanus, typhoid fever, diphtheria, syphilis, cholera, foodborne illness, leprosy and tuberculosis.
label: sentence

sentence: A pathogenic cause for a known medical disease may only be discovered many years after, as was the case with Helicobacter pylori and peptic ulcer disease.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacterial diseases are also important in agriculture, with bacteria causing leaf spot, fire blight and wilts in plants, as well as Johne's disease, mastitis, salmonella and anthrax in farm animals.
label: sentence

sentence: Each species of pathogen has a characteristic spectrum of interactions with its human hosts.
label: sentence

sentence: Some organisms, such as Staphylococcus or Streptococcus, can cause skin infections, pneumonia, meningitis and even overwhelming sepsis, a systemic inflammatory response producing shock, massive vasodilation and death.
label: sentence

sentence: Yet these organisms are also part of the normal human flora and usually exist on the skin or in the nose without causing any disease at all.
label: sentence

sentence: Other organisms invariably cause disease in humans, such as the Rickettsia, which are obligate intracellular parasites able to grow and reproduce only within the cells of other organisms.
label: sentence

sentence: One species of Rickettsia causes typhus, while another causes Rocky Mountain spotted fever.
label: sentence

sentence: Chlamydia, another phylum of obligate intracellular parasites, contains species that can cause pneumonia, or urinary tract infection and may be involved in coronary heart disease.
label: sentence

sentence: Finally, some species, such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Burkholderia cenocepacia, and Mycobacterium avium, are opportunistic pathogens and cause disease mainly in people suffering from immunosuppression or cystic fibrosis.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacterial infections may be treated with antibiotics, which are classified as bacteriocidal if they kill bacteria, or bacteriostatic if they just prevent bacterial growth.
label: sentence

sentence: There are many types of antibiotics and each class inhibits a process that is different in the pathogen from that found in the host.
label: sentence

sentence: An example of how antibiotics produce selective toxicity are chloramphenicol and puromycin, which inhibit the bacterial ribosome, but not the structurally different eukaryotic ribosome.
label: sentence

sentence: Antibiotics are used both in treating human disease and in intensive farming to promote animal growth, where they may be contributing to the rapid development of antibiotic resistance in bacterial populations.
label: sentence

sentence: Infections can be prevented by antiseptic measures such as sterilizing the skin prior to piercing it with the needle of a syringe, and by proper care of indwelling catheters.
label: sentence

sentence: Surgical and dental instruments are also sterilized to prevent contamination by bacteria.
label: sentence

sentence: Disinfectants such as bleach are used to kill bacteria or other pathogens on surfaces to prevent contamination and further reduce the risk of infection.
label: sentence

sentence: The ability of bacteria to degrade a variety of organic compounds is remarkable and has been used in waste processing and bioremediation.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria capable of digesting the hydrocarbons in petroleum are often used to clean up oil spills.
label: sentence

sentence: Fertilizer was added to some of the beaches in Prince William Sound in an attempt to promote the growth of these naturally occurring bacteria after the 1989 Exxon Valdez oil spill.
label: sentence

sentence: These efforts were effective on beaches that were not too thickly covered in oil.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria are also used for the bioremediation of industrial toxic wastes.
label: sentence

sentence: In the chemical industry, bacteria are most important in the production of enantiomerically pure chemicals for use as pharmaceuticals or agrichemicals.
label: sentence

sentence: Because of their ability to quickly grow and the relative ease with which they can be manipulated, bacteria are the workhorses for the fields of molecular biology, genetics and biochemistry.
label: sentence

sentence: By making mutations in bacterial DNA and examining the resulting phenotypes, scientists can determine the function of genes, enzymes and metabolic pathways in bacteria, then apply this knowledge to more complex organisms.
label: sentence

sentence: This aim of understanding the biochemistry of a cell reaches its most complex expression in the synthesis of huge amounts of enzyme kinetic and gene expression data into mathematical models of entire organisms.
label: sentence

sentence: This is achievable in some well-studied bacteria, with models of Escherichia coli metabolism now being produced and tested.
label: sentence

sentence: This understanding of bacterial metabolism and genetics allows the use of biotechnology to bioengineer bacteria for the production of therapeutic proteins, such as insulin, growth factors, or antibodies.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria were first observed by the Dutch microscopist Antonie van Leeuwenhoek in 1676, using a single-lens microscope of his own design.
label: sentence

sentence: He then published his observations in a series of letters to the Royal Society of London.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria were Leeuwenhoek's most remarkable microscopic discovery.
label: sentence

sentence: They were just at the limit of what his simple lenses could make out and, in one of the most striking hiatuses in the history of science, no one else would see them again for over a century.
label: sentence

sentence: Only then were his by-then-largely-forgotten observations of bacteria — as opposed to his famous "animalcules" (spermatozoa) — taken seriously.
label: sentence

sentence: Though it was known in the nineteenth century that bacteria are the cause of many diseases, no effective antibacterial treatments were available.
label: sentence

sentence: In 1910, Paul Ehrlich developed the first antibiotic, by changing dyes that selectively stained Treponema pallidum — the spirochaete that causes syphilis — into compounds that selectively killed the pathogen.
label: sentence

sentence: Ehrlich had been awarded a 1908 Nobel Prize for his work on immunology, and pioneered the use of stains to detect and identify bacteria, with his work being the basis of the Gram stain and the Ziehl–Neelsen stain.
label: sentence

sentence: When the board has no embedded components it is more correctly called a printed wiring board (PWB) or etched wiring board.
label: sentence

sentence: However, the term printed wiring board has fallen into disuse.
label: sentence

sentence: A PCB populated with electronic components is called a printed circuit assembly (PCA), printed circuit board assembly or PCB assembly (PCBA).
label: sentence

sentence: The IPC preferred term for assembled boards is circuit card assembly (CCA), and for assembled backplanes it is backplane assemblies.
label: sentence

sentence: The term PCB is used informally both for bare and assembled boards.
label: sentence

sentence: Initially PCBs were designed manually by creating a photomask on a clear mylar sheet, usually at two or four times the true size.
label: sentence

sentence: Starting from the schematic diagram the component pin pads were laid out on the mylar and then traces were routed to connect the pads.
label: sentence

sentence: Rub-on dry transfers of common component footprints increased efficiency.
label: sentence

sentence: Traces were made with self-adhesive tape.
label: sentence

sentence: Pre-printed non-reproducing grids on the mylar assisted in layout.
label: sentence

sentence: To fabricate the board, the finished photomask was photolithographically reproduced onto a photoresist coating on the blank copper-clad boards.
label: sentence

sentence: Panelization is a procedure whereby a number of PCBs are grouped for manufacturing onto a larger board - the panel.
label: sentence

sentence: Usually a panel consists of a single design but sometimes multiple designs are mixed on a single panel.
label: sentence

sentence: There are two types of panels: assembly panels - often called arrays - and bare board manufacturing panels.
label: sentence

sentence: The assemblers often mount components on panels rather than single PCBs because this is efficient.
label: sentence

sentence: The bare board manufactures always uses panels, not only for efficiency, but because of the requirements the plating process.
label: sentence

sentence: Thus a manufacturing panel can consist of a grouping of individual PCBs or of arrays, depending on what must be delivered.
label: sentence

sentence: The panel is eventually broken apart into individual PCBs; this is called depaneling.
label: sentence

sentence: Separating the individual PCBs is frequently aided by drilling or routing perforations along the boundaries of the individual circuits, much like a sheet of postage stamps.
label: sentence

sentence: Another method, which takes less space, is to cut V-shaped grooves across the full dimension of the panel.
label: sentence

sentence: The individual PCBs can then be broken apart along this line of weakness.
label: sentence

sentence: Today depaneling is often done by lasers which cut the board with no contact.
label: sentence

sentence: Laser panelization reduces stress on the fragile circuits.
label: sentence

sentence: Subtractive methods remove copper from an entirely copper-coated board to leave only the desired copper pattern.
label: sentence

sentence: In additive methods the pattern is electroplated onto a bare substrate using a complex process.
label: sentence

sentence: The advantage of the additive method is that less material is needed and less waste is produced.
label: sentence

sentence: In the full additive process the bare laminate is covered with a photosensitive film which is imaged (exposed to light through a mask and then developed which removes the unexposed film).
label: sentence

sentence: The exposed areas are sensitized in a chemical bath, usually containing palladium and similar to that used for through hole plating which makes the exposed area capable of bonding metal ions.
label: sentence

sentence: The laminate is then plated with copper in the sensitized areas.
label: sentence

sentence: When the mask is stripped, the PCB is finished.
label: sentence

sentence: Semi-additive is the most common process: The unpatterned board has a thin layer of copper already on it.
label: sentence

sentence: A reverse mask is then applied.
label: sentence

sentence: (Unlike a subtractive process mask, this mask exposes those parts of the substrate that will eventually become the traces.)
label: sentence

sentence: Additional copper is then plated onto the board in the unmasked areas; copper may be plated to any desired weight.
label: sentence

sentence: Tin-lead or other surface platings are then applied.
label: sentence

sentence: The mask is stripped away and a brief etching step removes the now-exposed bare original copper laminate from the board, isolating the individual traces.
label: sentence

sentence: Some single-sided boards which have plated-through holes are made in this way.
label: sentence

sentence: General Electric made consumer radio sets in the late 1960s using additive boards.
label: sentence

sentence: The simplest method, used for small-scale production and often by hobbyists, is immersion etching, in which the board is submerged in etching solution such as ferric chloride.
label: sentence

sentence: Compared with methods used for mass production, the etching time is long.
label: sentence

sentence: Heat and agitation can be applied to the bath to speed the etching rate.
label: sentence

sentence: In bubble etching, air is passed through the etchant bath to agitate the solution and speed up etching.
label: sentence

sentence: Splash etching uses a motor-driven paddle to splash boards with etchant; the process has become commercially obsolete since it is not as fast as spray etching.
label: sentence

sentence: In spray etching, the etchant solution is distributed over the boards by nozzles, and recirculated by pumps.
label: sentence

sentence: Adjustment of the nozzle pattern, flow rate, temperature, and etchant composition gives predictable control of etching rates and high production rates.
label: sentence

sentence: Multi-layer printed circuit boards have trace layers inside the board.
label: sentence

sentence: This is achieved by laminating a stack of materials in a press by applying pressure and heat for a period of time.
label: sentence

sentence: This results in an inseparable one piece product.
label: sentence

sentence: For example, a four-layer PCB can be fabricated by starting from a two-sided copper-clad laminate, etch the circuitry on both sides, then laminate to the top and bottom pre-preg and copper foil.
label: sentence

sentence: It is then drilled, plated, and etched again to get traces on top and bottom layers.
label: sentence

sentence: Holes through a PCB are typically drilled with small-diameter drill bits made of solid coated tungsten carbide.
label: sentence

sentence: Coated tungsten carbide is recommended since many board materials are very abrasive and drilling must be high RPM and high feed to be cost effective.
label: sentence

sentence: Drill bits must also remain sharp so as not to mar or tear the traces.
label: sentence

sentence: Drilling with high-speed-steel is simply not feasible since the drill bits will dull quickly and thus tear the copper and ruin the boards.
label: sentence

sentence: The drilling is performed by automated drilling machines with placement controlled by a drill tape or drill file.
label: sentence

sentence: These computer-generated files are also called numerically controlled drill (NCD) files or "Excellon files".
label: sentence

sentence: The drill file describes the location and size of each drilled hole.
label: sentence

sentence: The hole walls for boards with two or more layers can be made conductive and then electroplated with copper to form plated-through holes.
label: sentence

sentence: These holes electrically connect the conducting layers of the PCB.
label: sentence

sentence: For multi-layer boards, those with three layers or more, drilling typically produces a smear of the high temperature decomposition products of bonding agent in the laminate system.
label: sentence

sentence: Before the holes can be plated through, this smear must be removed by a chemical de-smear process, or by plasma-etch.
label: sentence

sentence: The de-smear process ensures that a good connection is made to the copper layers when the hole is plated through.
label: sentence

sentence: On high reliability boards a process called etch-back is performed chemically with a potassium permanganate based etchant or plasma.
label: sentence

sentence: The etch-back removes resin and the glass fibers so that the copper layers extend into the hole and as the hole is plated become integral with the deposited copper.
label: sentence

sentence: Matte solder is usually fused to provide a better bonding surface or stripped to bare copper.
label: sentence

sentence: Treatments, such as benzimidazolethiol, prevent surface oxidation of bare copper.
label: sentence

sentence: The places to which components will be mounted are typically plated, because untreated bare copper oxidizes quickly, and therefore is not readily solderable.
label: sentence

sentence: Traditionally, any exposed copper was coated with solder by hot air solder levelling (HASL).
label: sentence

sentence: The HASL finish prevents oxidation from the underlying copper, thereby guaranteeing a solderable surface.
label: sentence

sentence: This solder was a tin-lead alloy, however new solder compounds are now used to achieve compliance with the RoHS directive in the EU and US, which restricts the use of lead.
label: sentence

sentence: One of these lead-free compounds is SN100CL, made up of 99.3% tin, 0.7% copper, 0.05% nickel, and a nominal of 60ppm germanium.
label: sentence

sentence: Other platings used are OSP (organic surface protectant), immersion silver (IAg), immersion tin, electroless nickel with immersion gold coating (ENIG), electroless nickel electroless palladium immersion gold (ENEPIG) and direct gold plating (over nickel).
label: sentence

sentence: Edge connectors, placed along one edge of some boards, are often nickel plated then gold plated.
label: sentence

sentence: Another coating consideration is rapid diffusion of coating metal into Tin solder.
label: sentence

sentence: Tin forms intermetallics such as Cu5Sn6 and Ag3Cu that dissolve into the Tin liquidus or solidus(@50C), stripping surface coating or leaving voids.
label: sentence

sentence: Electrochemical migration (ECM) is the growth of conductive metal filaments on or in a printed circuit board (PCB) under the influence of a DC voltage bias.
label: sentence

sentence: Silver, zinc, and aluminum are known to grow whiskers under the influence of an electric field.
label: sentence

sentence: Silver also grows conducting surface paths in the presence of halide and other ions, making it a poor choice for electronics use.
label: sentence

sentence: Tin will grow "whiskers" due to tension in the plated surface.
label: sentence

sentence: Tin-Lead or solder plating also grows whiskers, only reduced by the percentage Tin replaced.
label: sentence

sentence: Reflow to melt solder or tin plate to relieve surface stress lowers whisker incidence.
label: sentence

sentence: Another coating issue is tin pest, the transformation of tin to a powdery allotrope at low temperature.
label: sentence

sentence: Areas that should not be soldered may be covered with solder resist (solder mask).
label: sentence

sentence: One of the most common solder resists used today is called "LPI" (liquid photoimageable solder mask).
label: sentence

sentence: A photo-sensitive coating is applied to the surface of the PWB, then exposed to light through the solder mask image film, and finally developed where the unexposed areas are washed away.
label: sentence

sentence: Dry film solder mask is similar to the dry film used to image the PWB for plating or etching.
label: sentence

sentence: After being laminated to the PWB surface it is imaged and develop as LPI.
label: sentence

sentence: Once common but no longer commonly used because of its low accuracy and resolution is to screen print epoxy ink.
label: sentence

sentence: Solder resist also provides protection from the environment.
label: sentence

sentence: Unpopulated boards are usually bare-board tested for "shorts" and "opens".
label: sentence

sentence: A short is a connection between two points that should not be connected.
label: sentence

sentence: An open is a missing connection between points that should be connected.
label: sentence

sentence: For high-volume production a fixture or a rigid needle adapter is used to make contact with copper lands on the board.
label: sentence

sentence: Building the adapter is a significant fixed cost and is only economical for high-volume or high-value production.
label: sentence

sentence: For small or medium volume production flying probe testers are used where test probes are moved over the board by an XY drive to make contact with the copper lands.
label: sentence

sentence: The CAM system instructs the electrical tester to apply a voltage to each contact point as required and to check that this voltage appears on the appropriate contact points and only on these.
label: sentence

sentence: Often, through-hole and surface-mount construction must be combined in a single assembly because some required components are available only in surface-mount packages, while others are available only in through-hole packages.
label: sentence

sentence: Another reason to use both methods is that through-hole mounting can provide needed strength for components likely to endure physical stress, while components that are expected to go untouched will take up less space using surface-mount techniques.
label: sentence

sentence: For further comparison, see the SMT page.
label: sentence

sentence: In boundary scan testing, test circuits integrated into various ICs on the board form temporary connections between the PCB traces to test that the ICs are mounted correctly.
label: sentence

sentence: Boundary scan testing requires that all the ICs to be tested use a standard test configuration procedure, the most common one being the Joint Test Action Group (JTAG) standard.
label: sentence

sentence: The JTAG test architecture provides a means to test interconnects between integrated circuits on a board without using physical test probes.
label: sentence

sentence: JTAG tool vendors provide various types of stimulus and sophisticated algorithms, not only to detect the failing nets, but also to isolate the faults to specific nets, devices, and pins.
label: sentence

sentence: PCBs intended for extreme environments often have a conformal coating, which is applied by dipping or spraying after the components have been soldered.
label: sentence

sentence: The coat prevents corrosion and leakage currents or shorting due to condensation.
label: sentence

sentence: The earliest conformal coats were wax; modern conformal coats are usually dips of dilute solutions of silicone rubber, polyurethane, acrylic, or epoxy.
label: sentence

sentence: Another technique for applying a conformal coating is for plastic to be sputtered onto the PCB in a vacuum chamber.
label: sentence

sentence: The chief disadvantage of conformal coatings is that servicing of the board is rendered extremely difficult.
label: sentence

sentence: Many assembled PCBs are static sensitive, and therefore must be placed in antistatic bags during transport.
label: sentence

sentence: When handling these boards, the user must be grounded (earthed).
label: sentence

sentence: Improper handling techniques might transmit an accumulated static charge through the board, damaging or destroying components.
label: sentence

sentence: Even bare boards are sometimes static sensitive.
label: sentence

sentence: Traces have become so fine that it's quite possible to blow an etch off the board (or change its characteristics) with a static charge.
label: sentence

sentence: This is especially true on non-traditional PCBs such as MCMs and microwave PCBs.
label: sentence

sentence: The first PCBs used through-hole technology, mounting electronic components by leads inserted through holes on one side of the board and soldered onto copper traces on the other side.
label: sentence

sentence: Boards may be single-sided, with an unplated component side, or more compact double-sided boards, with components soldered on both sides.
label: sentence

sentence: Horizontal installation of through-hole parts with two axial leads (such as resistors, capacitors, and diodes) is done by bending the leads 90 degrees in the same direction, inserting the part in the board (often bending leads located on the back of the board in opposite directions to improve the part's mechanical strength), soldering the leads, and trimming off the ends.
label: sentence

sentence: Leads may be soldered either manually or by a wave soldering machine.
label: sentence

sentence: Through-hole manufacture adds to board cost by requiring many holes to be drilled accurately, and limits the available routing area for signal traces on layers immediately below the top layer on multi-layer boards since the holes must pass through all layers to the opposite side.
label: sentence

sentence: Once surface-mounting came into use, small-sized SMD components were used where possible, with through-hole mounting only of components unsuitably large for surface-mounting due to power requirements or mechanical limitations, or subject to mechanical stress which might damage the PCB.
label: sentence

sentence: Surface-mount technology emerged in the 1960s, gained momentum in the early 1980s and became widely used by the mid-1990s.
label: sentence

sentence: Components were mechanically redesigned to have small metal tabs or end caps that could be soldered directly onto the PCB surface, instead of wire leads to pass through holes.
label: sentence

sentence: Components became much smaller and component placement on both sides of the board became more common than with through-hole mounting, allowing much smaller PCB assemblies with much higher circuit densities.
label: sentence

sentence: Surface mounting lends itself well to a high degree of automation, reducing labor costs and greatly increasing production rates.
label: sentence

sentence: Components can be supplied mounted on carrier tapes.
label: sentence

sentence: Surface mount components can be about one-quarter to one-tenth of the size and weight of through-hole components, and passive components much cheaper; prices of semiconductor surface mount devices (SMDs) are determined more by the chip itself than the package, with little price advantage over larger packages.
label: sentence

sentence: Some wire-ended components, such as 1N4148 small-signal switch diodes, are actually significantly cheaper than SMD equivalents.
label: sentence

sentence: Each trace consists of a flat, narrow part of the copper foil that remains after etching.
label: sentence

sentence: The resistance, determined by width and thickness, of the traces must be sufficiently low for the current the conductor will carry.
label: sentence

sentence: Power and ground traces may need to be wider than signal traces.
label: sentence

sentence: In a multi-layer board one entire layer may be mostly solid copper to act as a ground plane for shielding and power return.
label: sentence

sentence: For microwave circuits, transmission lines can be laid out in the form of stripline and microstrip with carefully controlled dimensions to assure a consistent impedance.
label: sentence

sentence: In radio-frequency and fast switching circuits the inductance and capacitance of the printed circuit board conductors become significant circuit elements, usually undesired; but they can be used as a deliberate part of the circuit design, obviating the need for additional discrete components.
label: sentence

sentence: The cloth or fiber material used, resin material, and the cloth to resin ratio determine the laminate's type designation (FR-4, CEM-1, G-10, etc.)
label: sentence

sentence: and therefore the characteristics of the laminate produced.
label: sentence

sentence: Important characteristics are the level to which the laminate is fire retardant, the dielectric constant (er), the loss factor (tδ), the tensile strength, the shear strength, the glass transition temperature (Tg), and the Z-axis expansion coefficient (how much the thickness changes with temperature).
label: sentence

sentence: There are quite a few different dielectrics that can be chosen to provide different insulating values depending on the requirements of the circuit.
label: sentence

sentence: Georgian architecture is the name given in most English-speaking countries to the set of architectural styles current between 1714 and 1830.
label: sentence

sentence: It is eponymous for the first four British monarchs of the House of Hanover—George I, George II, George III, and George IV—who reigned in continuous succession from August 1714 to June 1830.
label: sentence

sentence: The style was revived in the late 19th century in the United States as Colonial Revival architecture and in the early 20th century in Great Britain as Neo-Georgian architecture; in both it is also called Georgian Revival architecture.
label: sentence

sentence: In America the term "Georgian" is generally used to describe all building from the period, regardless of style; in Britain it is generally restricted to buildings that are "architectural in intention", and have stylistic characteristics that are typical of the period, though that covers a wide range.
label: sentence

sentence: The style of Georgian buildings is very variable, but marked by a taste for symmetry and proportion based on the classical architecture of Greece and Rome, as revived in Renaissance architecture.
label: sentence

sentence: Ornament is also normally in the classical tradition, but typically rather restrained, and sometimes almost completely absent on the exterior.
label: sentence

sentence: The period brought the vocabulary of classical architecture to smaller and more modest buildings than had been the case before, replacing English vernacular architecture (or becoming the new vernacular style) for almost all new middle-class homes and public buildings by the end of the period.
label: sentence

sentence: In towns, which expanded greatly during the period, landowners turned into property developers, and rows of identical terraced houses became the norm.
label: sentence

sentence: Even the wealthy were persuaded to live in these in town, especially if provided with a square of garden in front of the house.
label: sentence

sentence: There was an enormous amount of building in the period, all over the English-speaking world, and the standards of construction were generally high.
label: sentence

sentence: Where they have not been demolished, large numbers of Georgian buildings have survived two centuries or more, and they still form large parts of the core of cities such as London, Edinburgh, Dublin and Bristol.
label: sentence

sentence: The period saw the growth of a distinct and trained architectural profession; before the mid-century "the high-sounding title, 'architect' was adopted by anyone who could get away with it".
label: sentence

sentence: But most buildings were still designed by builders and landlords together, and the wide spread of Georgian architecture, and the Georgian styles of design more generally, came from dissemination through pattern books and inexpensive suites of engravings.
label: sentence

sentence: This contrasted with earlier styles, which were primarily disseminated among craftsmen through the direct experience of the apprenticeship system.
label: sentence

sentence: Authors such as the prolific William Halfpenny (active 1723–1755) received editions in America as well as Britain.
label: sentence

sentence: From the mid-18th century, Georgian styles were assimilated into an architectural vernacular that became part and parcel of the training of every architect, designer, builder, carpenter, mason and plasterer, from Edinburgh to Maryland.
label: sentence

sentence: Georgian succeeded the English Baroque of Sir Christopher Wren, Sir John Vanbrugh, Thomas Archer, William Talman, and Nicholas Hawksmoor; this in fact continued into at least the 1720s, overlapping with a more restrained Georgian style.
label: sentence

sentence: The architect James Gibbs was a transitional figure, his earlier buildings are Baroque, reflecting the time he spent in Rome in the early 18th century, but he adjusted his style after 1720.
label: sentence

sentence: Major architects to promote the change in direction from baroque were Colen Campbell, author of the influential book Vitruvius Britannicus (1715-1725); Richard Boyle, 3rd Earl of Burlington and his protégé William Kent; Isaac Ware; Henry Flitcroft and the Venetian Giacomo Leoni, who spent most of his career in England.
label: sentence

sentence: Other prominent architects of the early Georgian period include James Paine, Robert Taylor, and John Wood, the Elder.
label: sentence

sentence: The European Grand Tour became very common for wealthy patrons in the period, and Italian influence remained dominant, though at the start of the period Hanover Square, Westminster (1713 on), developed and occupied by Whig supporters of the new dynasty, seems to have deliberately adopted German stylisic elements in their honour, especially vertical bands connecting the windows.
label: sentence

sentence: The styles that resulted fall within several categories.
label: sentence

sentence: In the mainstream of Georgian style were both Palladian architecture— and its whimsical alternatives, Gothic and Chinoiserie, which were the English-speaking world's equivalent of European Rococo.
label: sentence

sentence: From the mid-1760s a range of Neoclassical modes were fashionable, associated with the British architects Robert Adam, James Gibbs, Sir William Chambers, James Wyatt, George Dance the Younger, Henry Holland and Sir John Soane.
label: sentence

sentence: John Nash was one of the most prolific architects of the late Georgian era known as The Regency style, he was responsible for designing large areas of London.
label: sentence

sentence: Greek Revival architecture was added to the repertory, beginning around 1750, but increasing in popularity after 1800.
label: sentence

sentence: Leading exponents were William Wilkins and Robert Smirke.
label: sentence

sentence: Georgian architecture is characterized by its proportion and balance; simple mathematical ratios were used to determine the height of a window in relation to its width or the shape of a room as a double cube.
label: sentence

sentence: Regularity, as with ashlar (uniformly cut) stonework, was strongly approved, imbuing symmetry and adherence to classical rules: the lack of symmetry, where Georgian additions were added to earlier structures remaining visible, was deeply felt as a flaw, at least before Nash began to introduce it in a variety of styles.

sentence: Regularity of housefronts along a street was a desirable feature of Georgian town planning.

sentence: Versions of revived Palladian architecture dominated English country house architecture.

sentence: Houses were increasingly placed in grand landscaped settings, and large houses were generally made wide and relatively shallow, largely to look more impressive from a distance.

sentence: The height was usually highest in the centre, and the Baroque emphasis on corner pavilions often found on the continent generally avoided.
