sentence: Among the vast varieties of microorganisms, relatively few cause disease in otherwise healthy individuals.
label: sentence

sentence: Infectious disease results from the interplay between those few pathogens and the defenses of the hosts they infect.
label: sentence

sentence: The appearance and severity of disease resulting from any pathogen, depends upon the ability of that pathogen to damage the host as well as the ability of the host to resist the pathogen.
label: sentence

sentence: However a host's immune system can also cause damage to the host itself in an attempt to control the infection.
label: sentence

sentence: Clinicians therefore classify infectious microorganisms or microbes according to the status of host defenses - either as primary pathogens or as opportunistic pathogens:
label: sentence

sentence: One way of proving that a given disease is "infectious", is to satisfy Koch's postulates (first proposed by Robert Koch), which demands that the infectious agent be identified only in patients and not in healthy controls, and that patients who contract the agent also develop the disease.
label: sentence

sentence: These postulates were first used in the discovery that Mycobacteria species cause tuberculosis.
label: sentence

sentence: Koch's postulates can not be applied ethically for many human diseases because they require experimental infection of a healthy individual with a pathogen produced as a pure culture.
label: sentence

sentence: Often, even clearly infectious diseases do not meet the infectious criteria.
label: sentence

sentence: For example, Treponema pallidum, the causative spirochete of syphilis, cannot be cultured in vitro - however the organism can be cultured in rabbit testes.
label: sentence

sentence: It is less clear that a pure culture comes from an animal source serving as host than it is when derived from microbes derived from plate culture.
label: sentence

sentence: Epidemiology is another important tool used to study disease in a population.
label: sentence

sentence: For infectious diseases it helps to determine if a disease outbreak is sporadic (occasional occurrence), endemic (regular cases often occurring in a region), epidemic (an unusually high number of cases in a region), or pandemic (a global epidemic).
label: sentence

sentence: Infectious diseases are sometimes called contagious disease when they are easily transmitted by contact with an ill person or their secretions (e.g., influenza).
label: sentence

sentence: Thus, a contagious disease is a subset of infectious disease that is especially infective or easily transmitted.
label: sentence

sentence: Other types of infectious/transmissible/communicable diseases with more specialized routes of infection, such as vector transmission or sexual transmission, are usually not regarded as "contagious", and often do not require medical isolation (sometimes loosely called quarantine) of victims.
label: sentence

sentence: However, this specialized connotation of the word "contagious" and "contagious disease" (easy transmissibility) is not always respected in popular use.
label: sentence

sentence: Infection begins when an organism successfully enters the body, grows and multiplies.
label: sentence

sentence: This is referred to as colonization.
label: sentence

sentence: Most humans are not easily infected.
label: sentence

sentence: Those who are weak, sick, malnourished, have cancer or are diabetic have increased susceptibility to chronic or persistent infections.
label: sentence

sentence: Individuals who have a suppressed immune system are particularly susceptible to opportunistic infections.
label: sentence

sentence: Entrance to the host at host-pathogen interface, generally occurs through the mucosa in orifices like the oral cavity, nose, eyes, genitalia, anus, or the microbe can enter through open wounds.
label: sentence

sentence: While a few organisms can grow at the initial site of entry, many migrate and cause systemic infection in different organs.
label: sentence

sentence: Some pathogens grow within the host cells (intracellular) whereas others grow freely in bodily fluids.
label: sentence

sentence: Wound colonization refers to nonreplicating microorganisms within the wound, while in infected wounds, replicating organisms exist and tissue is injured.
label: sentence

sentence: All multicellular organisms are colonized to some degree by extrinsic organisms, and the vast majority of these exist in either a mutualistic or commensal relationship with the host.
label: sentence

sentence: An example of the former is the anaerobic bacteria species, which colonizes the mammalian colon, and an example of the latter is various species of staphylococcus that exist on human skin.
label: sentence

sentence: Neither of these colonizations are considered infections.
label: sentence

sentence: The difference between an infection and a colonization is often only a matter of circumstance.
label: sentence

sentence: Non-pathogenic organisms can become pathogenic given specific conditions, and even the most virulent organism requires certain circumstances to cause a compromising infection.
label: sentence

sentence: Some colonizing bacteria, such as Corynebacteria sp.
label: sentence

sentence: and viridans streptococci, prevent the adhesion and colonization of pathogenic bacteria and thus have a symbiotic relationship with the host, preventing infection and speeding wound healing.
label: sentence

sentence: Because it is normal to have bacterial colonization, it is difficult to know which chronic wounds are infected.
label: sentence

sentence: Despite the huge number of wounds seen in clinical practice, there are limited quality data for evaluated symptoms and signs.
label: sentence

sentence: A review of chronic wounds in the Journal of the American Medical Association's "Rational Clinical Examination Series" quantified the importance of increased pain as an indicator of infection.
label: sentence

sentence: The review showed that the most useful finding is an increase in the level of pain [likelihood ratio (LR) range, 11-20] makes infection much more likely, but the absence of pain (negative likelihood ratio range, 0.64-0.88) does not rule out infection (summary LR 0.64-0.88).
label: sentence

sentence: Disease can arise if the host's protective immune mechanisms are compromised and the organism inflicts damage on the host.
label: sentence

sentence: Microorganisms can cause tissue damage by releasing a variety of toxins or destructive enzymes.
label: sentence

sentence: For example, Clostridium tetani releases a toxin that paralyzes muscles, and staphylococcus releases toxins that produce shock and sepsis.
label: sentence

sentence: Not all infectious agents cause disease in all hosts.
label: sentence

sentence: For example, less than 5% of individuals infected with polio develop disease.
label: sentence

sentence: On the other hand, some infectious agents are highly virulent.
label: sentence

sentence: The prion causing mad cow disease and Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease invariably kills all animals and people that are infected.
label: sentence

sentence: Persistent infections occur because the body is unable to clear the organism after the initial infection.
label: sentence

sentence: Persistent infections are characterized by the continual presence of the infectious organism, often as latent infection with occasional recurrent relapses of active infection.
label: sentence

sentence: There are some viruses that can maintain a persistent infection by infecting different cells of the body.
label: sentence

sentence: Some viruses once acquired never leave the body.
label: sentence

sentence: A typical example is the herpes virus, which tends to hide in nerves and become reactivated when specific circumstances arise.
label: sentence

sentence: Diagnosis of infectious disease sometimes involves identifying an infectious agent either directly or indirectly.
label: sentence

sentence: In practice most minor infectious diseases such as warts, cutaneous abscesses, respiratory system infections and diarrheal diseases are diagnosed by their clinical presentation and treated without knowledge of the specific causative agent.
label: sentence

sentence: Conclusions about the cause of the disease are based upon the likelihood that a patient came in contact with a particular agent, the presence of a microbe in a community, and other epidemiological considerations.
label: sentence

sentence: Given sufficient effort, all known infectious agents can be specifically identified.
label: sentence

sentence: The benefits of identification, however, are often greatly outweighed by the cost, as often there is no specific treatment, the cause is obvious, or the outcome of an infection is benign.
label: sentence

sentence: Diagnosis of infectious disease is nearly always initiated by medical history and physical examination.
label: sentence

sentence: More detailed identification techniques involve the culture of infectious agents isolated from a patient.
label: sentence

sentence: Culture allows identification of infectious organisms by examining their microscopic features, by detecting the presence of substances produced by pathogens, and by directly identifying an organism by its genotype.
label: sentence

sentence: Other techniques (such as X-rays, CAT scans, PET scans or NMR) are used to produce images of internal abnormalities resulting from the growth of an infectious agent.
label: sentence

sentence: The images are useful in detection of, for example, a bone abscess or a spongiform encephalopathy produced by a prion.
label: sentence

sentence: Microbiological culture is a principal tool used to diagnose infectious disease.
label: sentence

sentence: In a microbial culture, a growth medium is provided for a specific agent.
label: sentence

sentence: A sample taken from potentially diseased tissue or fluid is then tested for the presence of an infectious agent able to grow within that medium.
label: sentence

sentence: Most pathogenic bacteria are easily grown on nutrient agar, a form of solid medium that supplies carbohydrates and proteins necessary for growth of a bacterium, along with copious amounts of water.
label: sentence

sentence: A single bacterium will grow into a visible mound on the surface of the plate called a colony, which may be separated from other colonies or melded together into a "lawn".
label: sentence

sentence: The size, color, shape and form of a colony is characteristic of the bacterial species, its specific genetic makeup (its strain), and the environment that supports its growth.
label: sentence

sentence: Other ingredients are often added to the plate to aid in identification.
label: sentence

sentence: Plates may contain substances that permit the growth of some bacteria and not others, or that change color in response to certain bacteria and not others.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteriological plates such as these are commonly used in the clinical identification of infectious bacterium.
label: sentence

sentence: Microbial culture may also be used in the identification of viruses: the medium in this case being cells grown in culture that the virus can infect, and then alter or kill.
label: sentence

sentence: In the case of viral identification, a region of dead cells results from viral growth, and is called a "plaque".
label: sentence

sentence: Eukaryotic parasites may also be grown in culture as a means of identifying a particular agent.
label: sentence

sentence: In the absence of suitable plate culture techniques, some microbes require culture within live animals.
label: sentence

sentence: Bacteria such as Mycobacterium leprae and Treponema pallidum can be grown in animals, although serological and microscopic techniques make the use of live animals unnecessary.
label: sentence

sentence: Viruses are also usually identified using alternatives to growth in culture or animals.
label: sentence

sentence: Some viruses may be grown in embryonated eggs.
label: sentence

sentence: Another useful identification method is Xenodiagnosis, or the use of a vector to support the growth of an infectious agent.
label: sentence

sentence: Chagas disease is the most significant example, because it is difficult to directly demonstrate the presence of the causative agent, Trypanosoma cruzi in a patient, which therefore makes it difficult to definitively make a diagnosis.
label: sentence

sentence: In this case, xenodiagnosis involves the use of the vector of the Chagas agent T. cruzi, an uninfected triatomine bug, which takes a blood meal from a person suspected of having been infected.
label: sentence

sentence: The bug is later inspected for growth of T. cruzi within its gut.
label: sentence

sentence: Another principal tool in the diagnosis of infectious disease is microscopy.
label: sentence

sentence: Virtually all of the culture techniques discussed above rely, at some point, on microscopic examination for definitive identification of the infectious agent.
label: sentence

sentence: Microscopy may be carried out with simple instruments, such as the compound light microscope, or with instruments as complex as an electron microscope.
label: sentence

sentence: Samples obtained from patients may be viewed directly under the light microscope, and can often rapidly lead to identification.
label: sentence

sentence: Microscopy is often also used in conjunction with biochemical staining techniques, and can be made exquisitely specific when used in combination with antibody based techniques.
label: sentence

sentence: For example, the use of antibodies made artificially fluorescent (fluorescently labeled antibodies) can be directed to bind to and identify a specific antigens present on a pathogen.
label: sentence

sentence: A fluorescence microscope is then used to detect fluorescently labeled antibodies bound to internalized antigens within clinical samples or cultured cells.
label: sentence

sentence: This technique is especially useful in the diagnosis of viral diseases, where the light microscope is incapable of identifying a virus directly.
label: sentence

sentence: Other microscopic procedures may also aid in identifying infectious agents.
label: sentence

sentence: Almost all cells readily stain with a number of basic dyes due to the electrostatic attraction between negatively charged cellular molecules and the positive charge on the dye.
label: sentence

sentence: A cell is normally transparent under a microscope, and using a stain increases the contrast of a cell with its background.
label: sentence

sentence: Staining a cell with a dye such as Giemsa stain or crystal violet allows a microscopist to describe its size, shape, internal and external components and its associations with other cells.
label: sentence

sentence: The response of bacteria to different staining procedures is used in the taxonomic classification of microbes as well.
label: sentence

sentence: Two methods, the Gram stain and the acid-fast stain, are the standard approaches used to classify bacteria and to diagnosis of disease.
label: sentence

sentence: The Gram stain identifies the bacterial groups Firmicutes and Actinobacteria, both of which contain many significant human pathogens.
label: sentence

sentence: The acid-fast staining procedure identifies the Actinobacterial genera Mycobacterium and Nocardia.
label: sentence

sentence: The isolation of enzymes from infected tissue can also provide the basis of a biochemical diagnosis of an infectious disease.
label: sentence

sentence: For example, humans can make neither RNA replicases nor reverse transcriptase, and the presence of these enzymes are characteristic of specific types of viral infections.
label: sentence

sentence: The ability of the viral protein hemagglutinin to bind red blood cells together into a detectable matrix may also be characterized as a biochemical test for viral infection, although strictly speaking hemagglutinin is not an enzyme and has no metabolic function.
label: sentence

sentence: Serological methods are highly sensitive, specific and often extremely rapid tests used to identify microorganisms.
label: sentence

sentence: These tests are based upon the ability of an antibody to bind specifically to an antigen.
label: sentence

sentence: The antigen, usually a protein or carbohydrate made by an infectious agent, is bound by the antibody.
label: sentence

sentence: This binding then sets off a chain of events that can be visibly obvious in various ways, dependent upon the test.
label: sentence

sentence: For example, "Strep throat" is often diagnosed within minutes, and is based on the appearance of antigens made by the causative agent, S. pyogenes, that is retrieved from a patients throat with a cotton swab.
label: sentence

sentence: Serological tests, if available, are usually the preferred route of identification, however the tests are costly to develop and the reagents used in the test often require refrigeration.
label: sentence

sentence: Some serological methods are extremely costly, although when commonly used, such as with the "strep test", they can be inexpensive.
label: sentence

sentence: Complex serological techniques have been developed into what are known as Immunoassays.
label: sentence

sentence: Immunoassays can use the basic antibody – antigen binding as the basis to produce an electro - magnetic or particle radiation signal, which can be detected by some form of instrumentation.
label: sentence

sentence: Signal of unknowns can be compared to that of standards allowing quantitation of the target antigen.
label: sentence

sentence: To aid in the diagnosis of infectious diseases, immunoassays can detect or measure antigens from either infectious agents or proteins generated by an infected organism in response to a foreign agent.
label: sentence

sentence: For example, immunoassay A may detect the presence of a surface protein from a virus particle.
label: sentence

sentence: Immunoassay B on the other hand may detect or measure antibodies produced by an organism's immune system that are made to neutralize and allow the destruction of the virus.
label: sentence

sentence: Technologies based upon the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) method will become nearly ubiquitous gold standards of diagnostics of the near future, for several reasons.
label: sentence

sentence: First, the catalog of infectious agents has grown to the point that virtually all of the significant infectious agents of the human population have been identified.
label: sentence

sentence: Second, an infectious agent must grow within the human body to cause disease; essentially it must amplify its own nucleic acids in order to cause a disease.
label: sentence

sentence: This amplification of nucleic acid in infected tissue offers an opportunity to detect the infectious agent by using PCR.
label: sentence

sentence: Third, the essential tools for directing PCR, primers, are derived from the genomes of infectious agents, and with time those genomes will be known, if they are not already.
label: sentence

sentence: Thus, the technological ability to detect any infectious agent rapidly and specifically are currently available.
label: sentence

sentence: The only remaining blockades to the use of PCR as a standard tool of diagnosis are in its cost and application, neither of which is insurmountable.
label: sentence

sentence: The diagnosis of a few diseases will not benefit from the development of PCR methods, such as some of the clostridial diseases (tetanus and botulism).
label: sentence

sentence: These diseases are fundamentally biological poisonings by relatively small numbers of infectious bacteria that produce extremely potent neurotoxins.
label: sentence

sentence: A significant proliferation of the infectious agent does not occur, this limits the ability of PCR to detect the presence of any bacteria.
label: sentence

sentence: There is usually an indication for a specific identification of an infectious agent only when such identification can aid in the treatment or prevention of the disease, or to advance knowledge of the course of an illness prior to the development of effective therapeutic or preventative measures.
label: sentence

sentence: For example, in the early 1980s, prior to the appearance of AZT for the treatment of AIDS, the course of the disease was closely followed by monitoring the composition of patient blood samples, even though the outcome would not offer the patient any further treatment options.
label: sentence

sentence: In part, these studies on the appearance of HIV in specific communities permitted the advancement of hypotheses as to the route of transmission of the virus.
label: sentence

sentence: By understanding how the disease was transmitted, resources could be targeted to the communities at greatest risk in campaigns aimed at reducing the number of new infections.
label: sentence

sentence: The specific serological diagnostic identification, and later genotypic or molecular identification, of HIV also enabled the development of hypotheses as to the temporal and geographical origins of the virus, as well as a myriad of other hypothesis.
label: sentence

sentence: The development of molecular diagnostic tools have enabled physicians and researchers to monitor the efficacy of treatment with anti-retroviral drugs.
label: sentence

sentence: Molecular diagnostics are now commonly used to identify HIV in healthy people long before the onset of illness and have been used to demonstrate the existence of people who are genetically resistant to HIV infection.
label: sentence

sentence: Thus, while there still is no cure for AIDS, there is great therapeutic and predictive benefit to identifying the virus and monitoring the virus levels within the blood of infected individuals, both for the patient and for the community at large.

sentence: Techniques like hand washing, wearing gowns, and wearing face masks can help prevent infections from being passed from one person to another.
label: sentence

sentence: Frequent hand washing remains the most important defense against the spread of unwanted organisms.
label: sentence

sentence: There are other forms of prevention such as avoiding the use of illicit drugs, using a condom, and having a healthy lifestyle with a balanced diet and regular exercise.
label: sentence

sentence: Cooking foods well and avoiding foods that have been left outside for a long time is also important.
label: sentence

sentence: One of the ways to prevent or slow down the transmission of infectious diseases is to recognize the different characteristics of various diseases.
label: sentence

sentence: Some critical disease characteristics that should be evaluated include virulence, distance traveled by victims, and level of contagiousness.
label: sentence

sentence: The human strains of Ebola virus, for example, incapacitate their victims extremely quickly and kill them soon after.
label: sentence

sentence: As a result, the victims of this disease do not have the opportunity to travel very far from the initial infection zone.
label: sentence

sentence: Also, this virus must spread through skin lesions or permeable membranes such as the eye.
label: sentence

sentence: Thus, the initial stage of Ebola is not very contagious since its victims experience only internal hemorrhaging.
label: sentence

sentence: As a result of the above features, the spread of Ebola is very rapid and usually stays within a relatively confined geographical area.
label: sentence

sentence: In contrast, the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) kills its victims very slowly by attacking their immune system.
label: sentence

sentence: As a result, many of its victims transmit the virus to other individuals before even realizing that they are carrying the disease.
label: sentence

sentence: Also, the relatively low virulence allows its victims to travel long distances, increasing the likelihood of an epidemic.
label: sentence

sentence: Another effective way to decrease the transmission rate of infectious diseases is to recognize the effects of small-world networks.
label: sentence

sentence: In epidemics, there are often extensive interactions within hubs or groups of infected individuals and other interactions within discrete hubs of susceptible individuals.
label: sentence

sentence: Despite the low interaction between discrete hubs, the disease can jump to and spread in a susceptible hub via a single or few interactions with an infected hub.
label: sentence

sentence: Thus, infection rates in small-world networks can be reduced somewhat if interactions between individuals within infected hubs are eliminated (Figure 1).
label: sentence

sentence: However, infection rates can be drastically reduced if the main focus is on the prevention of transmission jumps between hubs.
label: sentence

sentence: The use of needle exchange programs in areas with a high density of drug users with HIV is an example of the successful implementation of this treatment method.

sentence: Another example is the use of ring culling or vaccination of potentially susceptible livestock in adjacent farms to prevent the spread of the foot-and-mouth virus in 2001.
label: sentence

sentence: Resistance to infection (immunity) may be acquired following a disease, by asymptomatic carriage of the pathogen, by harboring an organism with a similar structure (crossreacting), or by vaccination.

sentence: Knowledge of the protective antigens and specific acquired host immune factors is more complete for primary pathogens than for opportunistic pathogens.
label: sentence

sentence: There is also the phenomenon of herd immunity which offers a measure of protection to those otherwise vulnerable people when a large enough proportion of the population has acquired immunity from certain infections.

sentence: The clearance of the pathogens, either treatment-induced or spontaneous, it can be influenced by the genetic variants carried by the individual patients.
label: sentence

sentence: For instance, for genotype 1 hepatitis C treated with Pegylated interferon-alpha-2a or Pegylated interferon-alpha-2b (brand names Pegasys or PEG-Intron) combined with ribavirin, it has been shown that genetic polymorphisms near the human IL28B gene, encoding interferon lambda 3, are associated with significant differences in the treatment-induced clearance of the virus.

sentence: Myocardial infarction (MI) or acute myocardial infarction (AMI), commonly known as a heart attack, occurs when blood flow stops to a part of the heart causing damage to the heart muscle.
label: sentence

sentence: The most common symptom is chest pain or discomfort which may travel into the shoulder, arm, back, neck, or jaw.
label: sentence

sentence: Often it is in the center or left side of the chest and lasts for more than a few minutes.
label: sentence

sentence: The discomfort may occasionally feel like heartburn.
label: sentence

sentence: Other symptoms may include shortness of breath, nausea, feeling faint, a cold sweat, or feeling tired.
label: sentence

sentence: About 30% of people have atypical symptoms, with women more likely than men to present atypically.
label: sentence

sentence: Among those over 75 years old, about 5% have had an MI with little or no history of symptoms.
label: sentence

sentence: An MI may cause heart failure, an irregular heartbeat, or cardiac arrest.
label: sentence

sentence: Most MIs occur due to coronary artery disease.
label: sentence

sentence: Risk factors include high blood pressure, smoking, diabetes, lack of exercise, obesity, high blood cholesterol, poor diet, and excessive alcohol intake, among others.
label: sentence

sentence: The mechanism of an MI often involves the complete blockage of a coronary artery caused by a rupture of an atherosclerotic plaque.
label: sentence

sentence: MIs are less commonly caused by coronary artery spasms, which may be due to cocaine, significant emotional stress, and extreme cold, among others.
label: sentence

sentence: A number of tests are useful to help with diagnosis, including electrocardiograms (ECGs), blood tests, and coronary angiography.
label: sentence

sentence: An ECG may confirm an ST elevation MI if ST elevation is present.
label: sentence

sentence: Commonly used blood tests include troponin and less often creatine kinase MB.
label: sentence

sentence: Aspirin is an appropriate immediate treatment for a suspected MI.
label: sentence

sentence: Nitroglycerin or opioids may be used to help with chest pain; however, they do not improve overall outcomes.
label: sentence

sentence: Supplemental oxygen should be used in those with low oxygen levels or shortness of breath.
label: sentence

sentence: In ST elevation MIs treatments which attempt to restore blood flow to the heart are typically recommended and include angioplasty, where the arteries are pushed open, or thrombolysis, where the blockage is removed using medications.
label: sentence

sentence: People who have a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) are often managed with the blood thinner heparin, with the additional use angioplasty in those at high risk.
label: sentence

sentence: In people with blockages of multiple coronary arteries and diabetes, bypass surgery (CABG) may be recommended rather than angioplasty.
label: sentence

sentence: After an MI, lifestyle modifications, along with long term treatment with aspirin, beta blockers, and statins, are typically recommended.
label: sentence

sentence: The onset of symptoms in myocardial infarction (MI) is usually gradual, over several minutes, and rarely instantaneous.
label: sentence

sentence: Chest pain is the most common symptom of acute MI and is often described as a sensation of tightness, pressure, or squeezing.
label: sentence

sentence: Chest pain due to ischemia (a lack of blood and hence oxygen supply) of the heart muscle is termed angina pectoris.
label: sentence

sentence: Pain radiates most often to the left arm, but may also radiate to the lower jaw, neck, right arm, back, and upper abdomen, where it may mimic heartburn.
label: sentence

sentence: Levine's sign, in which a person localizes the chest pain by clenching their fists over their sternum, has classically been thought to be predictive of cardiac chest pain, although a prospective observational study showed it had a poor positive predictive value.
label: sentence

sentence: Shortness of breath occurs when the damage to the heart limits the output of the left ventricle, causing left ventricular failure and consequent pulmonary edema.
label: sentence

sentence: Other symptoms include diaphoresis (an excessive form of sweating), weakness, light-headedness, nausea, vomiting, and palpitations.
label: sentence

sentence: These symptoms are likely induced by a massive surge of catecholamines from the sympathetic nervous system, which occurs in response to pain and the blood flow abnormalities that result from dysfunction of the heart muscle.
label: sentence

sentence: Loss of consciousness (due to inadequate blood flow to the brain and cardiogenic shock) and sudden death (frequently due to the development of ventricular fibrillation) can occur in MIs.
label: sentence

sentence: Atypical symptoms are more frequently reported by women, the elderly, and those with diabetes when compared to their male and younger counterparts.
label: sentence

sentence: Women also report more numerous symptoms compared with men (2.6 on average vs. 1.8 symptoms in men).
label: sentence

sentence: The most common symptoms of MI in women include dyspnea, weakness, and fatigue.

sentence: Fatigue, sleep disturbances, and dyspnea have been reported as frequently occurring symptoms that may manifest as long as one month before the actual clinically manifested ischemic event.
label: sentence

sentence: In women, chest pain may be less predictive of coronary ischemia than in men.
label: sentence

sentence: Women may also experience back or jaw pain during an episode.

sentence: At least one quarter of all MIs are silent, without chest pain or other symptoms.

sentence: Estimates of the prevalence of silent MIs vary between 22 and 64%.

sentence: Acute myocardial infarction refers to two subtypes of acute coronary syndrome, namely non-ST-elevated and ST-elevated MIs, which are most frequently (but not always) a manifestation of coronary artery disease.

sentence: The most common triggering event is the disruption of an atherosclerotic plaque in an epicardial coronary artery, which leads to a clotting cascade, sometimes resulting in total occlusion of the artery.

sentence: Atherosclerosis is the gradual buildup of cholesterol and fibrous tissue in plaques in the wall of arteries (in this case, the coronary arteries), typically over decades.

sentence: Bloodstream column irregularities visible on angiography reflect artery lumen narrowing as a result of decades of advancing atherosclerosis.
